translation:
A basis in physical form is also necessary. Only through the gross form can one reach the subtle form. For the protection of King Ambarish, He was continuously present in subtle form. But when He came together with Rishi Durvasa to remove the curse, that was in an embodied form. Thus, that entity called Parbrahma, which is subtle and beyond even that, can remain simultaneously in subtle form and in embodied form. And whatever is embodied is also formless (nirgun), and this very formless one can, whenever needed, take on an embodied form in any shape. In seeing, in experience, or even in direct perception, illusion or ignorance can arise, and this direct experience can be false, or it can be true — this is a profound subject. Just as a rope lying in a dark room creates the illusion of a snake — even though seen directly, that knowledge is false; it is not a snake, only a rope. In the same way, one who has not gone beyond the outer senses cannot know and recognize Parbrahma. To recognize Him, one needs not the gross senses but His subtle essence. In the Mahabharata war, the gross senses were useless for beholding Krishna's universal form (Vishwarupa), so a subtle sense was granted to Arjuna. This same is the nature of Radha and Krishna. Who came to Ambarish's rescue for his protection? The name and form of that essence which came there has been shown by Jivanji Maharaj to be the Flute-Charming Supreme Lord (Morli Manohar Parmeshwar).

Why did Parbrahma have to come there Himself? Because it was on account of a Brahmin that He had to come. The name "Brahmin" too gives rise to a kind of ego, which is an outer worldly attachment (vasana). And because of this outer attachment, Durvasa made a mistake in recognizing Him. And the king, too, was overcome with ego. Thus, because of two opposing egos, both went astray. Earlier it was said in a sakhi that both the king and the sage were deceived — thus both went astray and both were deceived. To show how they were deceived, a beautiful sakhi is given here.

_amarikh gohare aaviyo. hari dharyo natvar vesh ||_
_sab jug bhulyo jeevana. karat anek anek ||29||_

(Meaning: Hari came to Ambarish's rescue and took on the guise of an actor — various forms and incarnations such as Krishna and so on. In this He has confused the entire world, and people come to see God as many, in numerous forms, and so they try to recognize Him through many incarnations and elements, and wander about in various places trying to find Him.)

Just as an actor in a bhavai (folk drama) puts on a different costume every day — one day he becomes a king, another day he becomes a pauper — Parbrahma is just like that actor. According to need, He comes in whatever guise (birth) is required and departs again, and out of all this, only very few souls are able to recognize Him. The rest of the world wanders here and there trying to recognize Him, yet they cannot know Him. Thus Parbrahma is one and the same; only the guise changes. But if, letting go of Parbrahma, one clings only to the guise, the soul cannot be freed — that is, it falls into a lower state. Therefore, leaving aside the various guises, one should recognize only that original, root essence. Just as an actor may sometimes take on the guise of King Bhoj, but because of that he cannot actually remove anyone's suffering — because once the intoxication of the role wears off, he himself becomes poor again. This is why the names and forms Ram and Krishna alone are such that they can grant the soul a vision of Parbrahma's true form. What happens if the soul falls into doubt and confusion (dagdago)? The Bhagavat Mahatmya, chapter 2, verse 20, says:

_bhaktidrohakara ye cha te sidanti jagatraye ||_
_durvasa duhkham aapannah pura bhaktir vinindakah ||18||_

(Meaning: Those who commit treachery against devotion suffer in the three worlds, just as Durvasa suffered for once disparaging devotion.)

_aave aave re govaliyani sange ramato ||_
_sange ramato more man gamato ||1||_

In this malgodi song, Narsinh Mehta sings on seeing Shri Krishna approaching him. According to the story, once his son-in-law asked Narsinh Mehta: "Bhagat, you are a beloved devotee of God, and you have seen Krishna — will you not show Him to me?" The devotee said, "Certainly, I will grant you His vision." So one day both walked together, going far out into the wilderness, where, seeing God approaching from the opposite direction in the guise of a cowherd, Mehtaji burst into song, but the son-in-law could not recognize Him and began mocking Mehtaji, saying he had made an ordinary cowherd out to be the real Krishna. Thus, one who looks only at the outer guise remains confused and deceived, and the soul does not attain God.

_das avatarke dag dage. bhulya sab sansar ||_
_ko ek ugare jeevana. jine guru mukh kiyo vichar ||30||_

(Meaning: Because of confusion over which of God's ten incarnations to worship, all the people of the world fell into confusion and error. But those who received true understanding from a guru and, understanding the true essence of God, engaged in devotion to Him, were saved.)

For those who fall into confusion over which of these ten incarnations to worship, the Parchari (biography) of Krishnadas says:

_kaustubh mani mukh morli, sundar shyam sharir ||_
_so nanddware jeevana, je dashrath kul badvir ||29||_

(Meaning: He who wears the Kaustubh jewel and holds the flute at His mouth, whose body is beautifully dark-hued, that very One who became a great hero born in Dashrath's lineage, sports in Nanda's court as Krishna.)

_ehi roop hirdeme dharo, ehi naam rasana uchaaro ||_
_inki chhaya moorat karahi, sab koi moortakun anusarahi ||_
_mool chhand chhayakun dhyave, aad roop bisar hi jave ||_
_aad roop hirdemein dharo, taako naam rasana uchaaro ||_
_ese tokun kahi nishani, aur baat kahun man mani ||_
_kou machharoopku dhyave, koo kachhapkun batave ||_
_koo seetakun man lave, koo ram lakshman gun gave ||_
_koo radhe radhe karahi, koo girdhari chit dharahi ||_
_hamare ram krishna do nama, guru kripaye sarahi kaama ||_
(Krishnadas Parchari)

(Meaning: Hold this form of Ram-Krishna, adorned with the Kaustubh jewel and the flute, within your heart, and chant only His name with your tongue. But people make idols of His shadow-illusion form, and everyone follows these idols in devotion — leaving God's original form and worshipping His shadow-maya, the form of an incarnation, thereby forgetting God's original form. But we should keep only God's primal original form within our hearts and utter and worship His name with the tongue. Thus I have explained to you the sign of God's true form as against His maya-shadow form; but let me also speak of those who worship God according to their own mind's fancy, imagining various invented forms. In their minds some worship the form of the Fish incarnation, some regard the Tortoise incarnation as their object of worship, while others keep Sita in mind, and some sing the praises of Ram and Lakshman in devotion. Still others worship by chanting "Radhe Radhe," while others mentally worship the form of Girdhari Krishna, the lifter of Govardhan. But truly, for us, only these two names — Ram and Krishna — are worthy of worship; by the guru's grace, remembering and reciting this name will accomplish the work of crossing the ocean of worldly existence — not the worship of His various other forms.)

_avatar apradhi kahe jeevana. jaake nahi guru pir ||_
_aadi ant madhya shyamalo. nirgun brahma sharir ||31||_

Pir-Samarth — one who has not found a capable guru mistakes the incarnations for God and goes astray, taking the incarnation itself to be God. But before, during, and after any incarnation, the dark-complexioned Krishna Himself is present in every state. He, the Supreme Being, alone is real; but deluded, offending people take even this Ram-Krishna to be among these ten incarnations. Yet this Ram-Krishna, before these incarnations occur, during the incarnation, and after the incarnation, remains without any change whatsoever, exactly as He is, in His own original form. Therefore this Ram-Krishna must be counted apart from — excluded from — the Ram-Krishna figures found among these ten incarnations. They should be recognized not by form but by name.

The world, which is not guided by a guru, has fallen into confusion over talk of incarnations, and such a worldly soul does not cross over; only the one guided by a guru, who places faith in the guru's words, crosses over.

_nagara mil baatan kare. kahe ram krishna avatar ||_
_aur gaali kaha jeevana. dhik taako parivar ||32||_

(Meaning: Worthless, deceitful people gather and talk among themselves, saying that Ram and Krishna are also merely incarnations, and that they themselves are Brahm. They ask: then why should Ram-Krishna not likewise be regarded as Parbrahma? The answer is that this Ram-Krishna is not Brahm merely by body, but is indeed Parbrahma in consciousness; and if one says Ram-Krishna is not Parbrahma, then Jivanji Maharaj says: what greater curse could be given to such people — their entire family is to be condemned, because Ram-Krishna is verily Parbrahma manifest, and therefore should not be counted among the ten incarnations.)

Those who have not taken a guru are called "guru-less" (nugra). They cannot recognize the true Name and Form, and so they come to regard the names Ram and Krishna as false talk about mere incarnations. This is a very great curse upon them. What worse insult could there be for them? Such an entire family is to be condemned.

"If one worships Ram and Krishna, the soul crosses over; of what use is it to remember and chant the mantra of other incarnations? Worship of other incarnations does not serve the purpose."

Meaning: If one worships Ram and Krishna, the soul crosses over. Ram and Krishna are not merely incarnated great persons, but are the very name of the formless, unblemished Parbrahma. That is: the Puranic scriptures contain various kinds of stories, in which, along with many incarnations, various mantras, vows, fasts, the greatness of holy places, and also various stories about the lives and deeds of different gods and goddesses are given. Moreover, not all the Puranas together lead to one single, fixed goal, nor is there a single agreed opinion among them. The Vishnu-based Puranas hold Vishnu to be the Lord of all; the Shiva-based Puranas hold Shiva so; the Devi Puranas hold Shakti or Devi worship so; and so on — thus there is no single agreed view among these various stories. Furthermore, what is the point of confusing ordinary people and keeping them far from truth through various mantras, tantras, and modes of worship? Thus Jivanji Maharaj, setting aside the fascinating stories of the incarnations and without entering into any dispute, suggests only the remembrance of the one Name and pure worship of Parbrahma with body and mind.

Thus, without considering all the other paths, one should proceed by only the one path. Jivanji Maharaj does not wish to engage in any scriptural debate on this subject, nor does he wish to trouble anyone who holds an opposing view. Rather, he wishes to find his own path from among all these and proceed along it. Those who have faith in the words of the guru should keep that faith and follow accordingly. Here, the conclusion or summary of the dialogue that took place between Guru Gopaldas and Jivanji Maharaj has been presented. The part that consisted of debate and dispute has not been included anywhere here. Because once the truth has been found, there is no purpose in dwelling on falsehood. Jivanji Maharaj obtained what he needed, so only that essential matter has been presented here, and that too has been stated very concisely. Rather than wasting time on useless talk, he has conveyed only the essential matter — words whose very utterance changes the dignity of the atmosphere, brings a wave of loving devotion, and gladdens the mind. Useless matters have not been told to the devotees; in a single sentence he said what needed to be said: that other incarnations did not serve the purpose — that is, one need not get involved with other incarnations or their stories, nor is it worth recalling them here. Having said this, concluding this discussion, he states a sakhi:

_ram krishna je jeevana. do sagun avatar ||_
_andh dhandh kaha bhaju. je ved na pave paar ||33||_

Parbrahma's two names, Ram and Krishna, are also given in the Puranas as the story of two incarnations with attributes (sagun). But one should not blindly plunge, eyes closed, into the illusion-shadowed, disordered other incarnations, because even the Vedas know nothing about Parbrahma — even they are ignorant of Him. Therefore one should not fall into the worship of any deity without proper understanding and reflection.

Here is a sakhi of Baba Kabirji:

_kabir saayi hamara ramji. jaaka dashrath baap ||_
_duniyakun dojakh diya. hamkun apna jaap ||34||_

_kabir bavan akshar teen lokman. unka sab vistar ||_
_unthi je uparant hai. so niranjan nirakar ||35||_

Meaning: Kabirji says that many people argue at length over the name of Ram. Such learned people remain absorbed only in disputation and thereby suffer — that is, they fall into hell. But for us, it is one name of Parbrahma, which we recite in remembrance.

The maya of Brahma pervades the fifty-two letters and all three worlds, and deluded people worship this, thinking it to be Parbrahma. But beyond that — that is, beyond maya — is the formless, unblemished Parbrahma.

God's ten incarnations are counted, but among them we worship only Ram and Krishna. Moreover, if for some separate fancy one remembers, worships, or chants the mantra of another incarnation, it is of no use — other incarnations do not serve the purpose, that is, they are of no use in crossing the ocean of existence. In keeping with this, Jivanji Maharaj states this sakhi: that Ram and Krishna are the two manifest, embodied forms of God with attributes. All the other incarnations are disordered and illusory, through which one cannot gain a true realization of God as He really is; therefore Jivanji Maharaj declares those other incarnations to be avoided. But the two principal incarnations, Ram and Krishna, are the exact, fitting, complete Purushottam form of God. Therefore worship of them brings well-being. Moreover, these attribute-bearing incarnations should not be regarded as equal to the other incarnations, because even these incarnations of Ram and Krishna carry God's shadow (maya) — whereas the form of Ram and Krishna, though possessing attributes, is beyond maya. In support of this view, Sadguru Jivanji Maharaj presents the 19th sakhi of Kabirji's Das Ang, saying:

_saayi hamaara raamji_ (a variant reading),

_thakur hamara ramji, jaaka dashrath baap_ — such statements might seem self-contradictory, but here Kabirji explains through the 14th sakhi of the Agadhko Ang that although the name of God taken in the three worlds is limited to the fifty-two letters of the alphabet, the name of Parbrahma is not bound by the limits of the letters of any alphabet. He is beyond even speech, unutterable by words — that formless, unblemished Supreme Being who is Ram-Krishna. Even though, in His attribute-bearing form, He may be called the son of a father like Dashrath, yet His true parentage, in the context of Ram, cannot actually be stated in words. The world knows Dashrath as the father of Ram; and this misleads worldly people about Ram. Because of this, taking Him to be merely the son of Dashrath, they go to hell.

Whether to count Ram and Krishna among the ten attribute-bearing, embodied incarnations, or to regard them as beyond these, is a point of confusion. Kabirji too, in his sakhis, has shown this very confusion and resolved it. This is worth understanding: Kabirji means to say that Ram has misled the world.

_nagar ayodhya rai tum, bhaye anek hi vaar ||_
_apni aadi bhulaviya, tum kaise keertaar ||30||_

Kabir says: You have become the king of Ayodhya city, called the Lord of Ayodhya, age after age, many times over, and you make the people of the world forget your true original form as the Supreme Being — what kind of Creator of the world are you, then?

Sadguru Jivanji Maharaj says the same:

_guru kije vicharke, jehi batave ram ||_
_sarjutire jeevana, nagar ayodhya gaam ||31||_
_saayi hamaran ramji, jaake bharat shatrughna bhrat ||_
_shankarshan sang janaki, jeevan e jag taat ||32||_

Jivanji Maharaj says: You should choose as your guru, after careful consideration, one who shows you the true Ram — the Ram who lived on the banks of the river Saryu, in the town called Ayodhya.

Moreover, my object of worship is Ram, whose brothers are Bharat and Shatrughna, and who is accompanied by Lakshman and Sitaji — He is the father of the world.

_sadguru-e samjhaayo jeevana, tab bhayo man dheer ||_
_pay paayo deval phiro, tab yu kahi das kabir ||33||_

When the Sadguru explained the true understanding of devotion to such a Ram, my mind became assured that this is the same Ram who drank Namdev's milk and turned the temple around — so says Das Kabir. Meaning: this Ram directly drinks milk for His devotee and even turns the direction of a temple — such a capable ruler of the world is He. That very Ram, whom the people of the world regard as the Ram of Ayodhya on the banks of the Saryu, is the same Ram who, in Pandharpur, drank milk for a devotee like Namdev and turned the temple — showing that God can also take on a manifest, embodied form. This Ram possesses both name and form. That is why Kabir has said:

_kabir sagun to ek sant hai, nirgun naam aadhaar ||_
_nirgun sagunmein mil rahya, tab bhayo ek vichaar ||34||_

Kabirji says: God is with attributes (sagun) in the form of the saint, and without attributes (nirgun) on the basis of Name and Form. Thus, when the nirgun Name merges into the sagun saint whom the devotee worships, sagun and nirgun become one, and there is then no need to consider any distinction between nirgun and sagun.

Thus Kabir said that Ram, whose father is Dashrath, is his object of worship. Furthermore, Jivanji Maharaj firmly declared that Ram, on the banks of the Saryu, is together with Sita, and has Lakshman, Shatrughna, and Bharat as brothers. But the devotee can make the nirgun Ram into sagun and even make Him drink milk — so what is to be said of such a Ram? In this connection, Anantdas, in the Parchari of Ranka Vanka, has said:

_pay paayo deval phiro. bhakti na aayi tohe ||_
_sant poojare naamdev. jo miliya chaahe mohe ||35||_

You made Me drink milk, and for you I turned My temple, yet even so, you did not attain devotion to that God who is formless and without attributes. Therefore God says: if you wish to meet Me, serve the saints — do not seek Me in this idol. So He tells Namdev in the Ranka Vanka.

Kabirji has said that God is beyond the three gunas (qualities):

_kabir nugara nar sanse padya. suni nahi gurumukh baat ||_
_trigun ateet niradhaar hai. so dashrathsut raghuveer ||36||_

That Ram who is called the son of Dashrath is truly beyond the three gunas — this understanding, not having heard the guru's teaching, guru-less people failed to grasp; and so they fell into doubt, taking Him to merely be Dashrath's boy. Kabir says —

_raam naam sab kahat hai. so to naam ameer ||_
_ajar amar ek raam hai. vaaku jape kabir ||37||_

Everyone speaks the name of Ram as they please, in the ordinary way, but that name of Ram is filled with deep mystery. There is one Ram who is ageless and immortal — it is Him that Kabirji worships.

The Parchari of Krishnadas says:

_kabir saacha sadguru jab mile. to sat bataave raam ||_
_sarju teere khelke. aayo gokul gaam ||38||_

If one finds a Sadguru who explains the true Ram, he will show how to worship the true Ram — the Ram who sported on the banks of the Saryu at Ayodhya and who came as Krishna in Gokul. This means there is no distinction between Krishna and Ram. If one obtains a guru who has this correct understanding, he will make it clear to us that there is no difference between Ram and Krishna. Only a true Sadguru gives the understanding that Ram and Krishna are the manifest form of Parbrahma — not that he says they are merely incarnations. Jivanji Maharaj says —

_sadguru-e samjhaayo jeevana. gupt pragat je baat ||_
_ek roop ghat ghat base. ek seetapati raghunath ||39||_
(Gurudev 40)

The Sadguru has made clear the true reality of Ram — that Ram who exists manifest with attributes, or who remains hidden, formless. In one form Ram pervades every heart, and in one form Ram remains as the husband of Sita. In the Vicharak Ang, Kabir says:

_kabir raam raam sabko kahe. taame bohot vichaar ||_
_sohi raam sati saadhu kahe. sohi kautuk haar ||40||_

Everyone says "Ram, Ram," but there is a great deal to consider in how it is said. Behold — one, by uttering the name Ram, rises to sainthood, while another who merely watches this Ram as a spectacle calls it a mere show.

_kabir bhaand bhavaai dugaliya. sabko kahe raam ||_
_satnaam jaanya vina. kis vidh sare kaam ||41||_

Bards, minstrels, folk-actors, and jugglers — all of them say "Ram, Ram." But without knowing the true Name, how can their purpose be accomplished? How can they attain liberation?

_kabir ek raam dashrath ghar dole. ek raam sab ghatmein baale ||_
_ek raamka sakal pasaara. ek raam tinguNse nyaara ||42||_

One Ram wanders in Dashrath's house; a second speaks within every heart; a third Ram's expanse pervades everything; a fourth Ram is entirely apart from the three gunas.

_kabir kaun raam dashrath ghar dole. kaun raam ghatghatmein bole ||_
_kaun raamka saphal pasaara. kaun raam tinguNse nyaara ||43||_

Which Ram wanders in Dashrath's house? And which Ram speaks in every heart? And which Ram pervades everything? And which Ram is apart from the three gunas?

_aakaar raam dashrath ghar dole. niraakaar ghatghatmein bole ||_
_niranjan raamka sakal pasaara. niraalamb raam sabhise nyaara ||44||_

The embodied Ram wanders in Dashrath's house; the formless one, as the breath-form soul, speaks in every heart; the point-like unblemished Ram extends everywhere; and the unsupported, pure-consciousness Ram is apart from all.

Thus Ram is described in four ways, but in the end a single conclusion is given for all:

_kabir sohi raam sab ghatme bole. sohi raam dashrath ghar dole ||_
_sohi raamka sakal pasaara. sohi raam sabhise nyaara ||45||_

Though Ram is spoken of in four ways, it is this one and the same Ram who speaks in every heart, and it is this same Ram who wanders in Dashrath's house; likewise it is this same Ram who pervades everything, and this same Ram who is apart from all.

_kabir suno bhaai saadho. nij naamke e chaaro ||_
_chotha raam sada avinaashi. kahe kabir vichaar ||46||_

Listen, O saints — these four are the names of one's own self; among them, the fourth kind of Ram is eternally imperishable — so says Kabir, having reflected and understood.

_kabir saahab mera ek hai. dooja kaha na jaay ||_
_dooja saahab jo kahu. saahab khara risaay ||47||_

My Lord, my object of worship, is one alone; it cannot be said that there is a second Lord. And if I say there is a second Lord, the true Lord would be displeased, and I would lose His true devotion. Further, in the Bijak, in verse ("shabda") 30 — or 26 — it is said:

_bhai re dui jagdeesh kahaanse aaya, kahu kavne bauraaya ||_

Sadguru Kabir says: O brother, from where have two Lords of the universe come? Tell me — who has driven you into such delusion?

_kabir saahab sabka baap hai. beta kisika naahi ||_
_beta hokar avatare. so to saahab naahi ||48||_

God is the father of all; He is no one's son. If He were to be born incarnate as a son, then He would not be the true Lord.

In our lives we jokingly ask small children whose child they are — their father's or their mother's. In truth, a son does not belong exclusively to either the father or the mother. In the same way, then, how is it proper to call a God like Ram the son of Dashrath? In fact, the intent of saying "Dashrath" is that the one whom people take to be the son of Dashrath is actually the wondrous, playful Ram of God. Therefore, one should not fall into confusion, taking "whose father is Dashrath" to mean an ordinary incarnate Ram.

_nij karta avatar dharat nahi. mrityu lokke chole ||_
_jinka karta sakal kul hovat. so to kyu ghar ghar dole ||49||_

Meaning: God Himself, the Creator of the universe, having taken an incarnation in a body in the mortal world, is the Creator of the entire creation — why, then, should He wander from house to house, from birth to birth?

Now let us explain the qualities and pastimes (leela) of Ram and Krishna that have been spoken of. That is, let us here explain in detail the pastimes described in the great Bhagavat Purana.

_kab raghupati kab jadupati. bhagat het avatar ||_
_bemukh nav samjhe jeevana. e sab ekaakaar ||36||_
_dhanurvidya raghupati padhe. morli dhari jadunath ||_
_lankeshwar maarya jeevana. giri dharya ve haath ||37||_

Meaning: Sometimes as Raghupati King Ram, sometimes as Yadupati Shri Krishna — He took birth for the sake of His devotees. But those turned away from Him, the faithless, do not understand that both these forms belong to one and the same Supreme Being.

King Ram studied the art of archery and bore that weapon, while Shri Krishna bore the flute. With the very same hands with which Parbrahma slew Ravana, the lord of Lanka, He also lifted Mount Govardhan. That is, in terms of embodied form, these two incarnations are different, but for the devotee who sees the formless, attributeless reality, there is no difference or wonder in this — it is merely Parbrahma's action, His leela (divine play). This is merely Parbrahma's "play." Kabirji says —

In Raag Kalyan (Bhairav):

_raghupati jadupati ki bal jaau, de dhare payo hari naanu ||_
_raghupati vanme kino vaas, jadupati mathura nagar nivaas ||tek||_
_raghupati vaanar rinch milai, jadupati gopi gwal khelai ||_
_raghupati charne ahalya taari, jadupati kubja adhik sohai ||1||_
_raghupati shaayar paaj bandhai, jadupati govardhan kar dhaari ||_
_raghupati raavan maar liyo, jadupati kans nikandan kiyo ||2||_
_raghupati raaj bibhishan diyo, jadupati ugrasenkun raaj diyo ||_
_raghupati jadupati ek sharira, het kari gaave das kabira ||3||_

Kabirji says: I offer myself to Raghupati and Jadupati (Ram and Krishna); taking on a body, they bore these two names, Ram and Krishna, and through both forms they performed, in nearly the same way, the work of creation. Raghupati dwelt in the forest, Jadupati dwelt in the city of Mathura. Raghupati gathered together monkeys and bears, Jadupati sported with the gopis and cowherds. Raghupati redeemed Ahalya at His feet, Jadupati was greatly adorned with Kubja. Raghupati had a bridge built across the ocean, Jadupati lifted Govardhan in His hand. Raghupati slew Ravana, Jadupati destroyed Kansa. Raghupati gave the kingdom to Vibhishan, Jadupati gave the kingdom to Ugrasen. Raghupati and Jadupati are one and the same body — with love, Das Kabir sings of them.

Related to this pada of Kabirji, a pada of Parashuram expressing the oneness of Ram and Krishna has been given in the Samagam. In this pada, the non-difference between Krishna and Ram is shown. When Tulsidas went to the place named Gyan Gudri, at the temple of Madan Gopal, Shri Krishna was adorned — with the flute, with the staff, with the peacock-feather crown upon His head, with the garland worn on His chest, and standing close to Radhaji, the stealer of hearts — such was the threefold-bending (tribhangi) image that shone there. One day, as Tulsidasji was preparing to prostrate himself, a worshipper of Krishna recited to him this doha of Parashuram:

_apne apne ishtako naman karai sab koi ||_
_isht viheene parashuram namai so moorakh hoi ||50||_

Everyone bows to their own chosen deity. But Parashuram says: whoever bows to someone other than his chosen deity is a fool.

So Tulsidas grew alarmed, and in response he says:

_parashuraamke vachan suni maanat hiye hulaas ||_
_seetaravan samaarike bole tulsidas ||51||_

Hearing these words of Parashuram's sakhi, and bringing joy to his heart, Tulsidas, holding fast in his mind to Sita's Lord (Ram), spoke these words.

_kaha kahau chhabi aajki bhale bane ho naath ||_
_tulsi mastak jab navai dharo dhanush shar haath ||52||_

O Lord! What can I say of today's beauty — you look very handsome indeed. But Tulsidas will only bow his head to you when you take up the bow and arrow in your hand.

_mor mugat neeche dharo. kanakmugat dharo sees ||_
_dhanushbaan kar dharo. tab tulsi name sees ||53||_

Set aside the peacock-feather crown, wear the golden crown on your head, take up bow and arrow in your hand — then Tulsidas will bow his head to you.

_tulsi teri tekkun. dhan kahat raghunath ||_
_dhanush baan jab kare dharo. tab tulsi naayo maath ||54||_

The Lord says: Tulsidas, blessed be your steadfastness. When the Lord took up the bow and arrow, Tulsidas bowed his head.

_murli lakut duraaikai. dharyo dhanush shar haath ||_
_tulsi lakhi ruchi daaski. naath bhaye raghunath ||55||_

Setting aside the flute and the staff, He took up the bow and arrow in His hand. Thus, understanding and honoring the wish of His devotee Tulsidas, Lord Krishna took on the form of Ram.

_kit murli kit chandrika, kit gopiyanke saath ||_
_apne janke kaarane, krishna bhaye raghunath ||56||_

Where is Krishna's flute, where the peacock-crown's moonlight, where His sporting with the gopis — for the sake of His own devotee, Krishna became Raghunath (Ram). Writing Tulsidas's life story, Veni Madhavdas has written thus:

_vipra naabha sahit hari darshanke het._
_gaye gusaai mudit man mohanmadan niket ||1||_
_raam upaasak jaani prabhu turat dhare dhanu baan ||_
_darshan diye sanaath kiye, bhakt vachhal bhagvaan ||2||_

Tulsidas, along with the Brahmin Nabha, went joyfully with delight in his heart to have darshan of Hari at the beautiful abode of the enchanting Madan Gopal. Then, recognizing him as a worshipper of Ram, the Lord immediately took up the bow and arrow, gave him His darshan, made him feel cared for, and thus the Lord, who is affectionate to His devotees, fulfilled him.

About this incident of Tulsidas, Revered Yadunath Maharaj writes: devotion cannot happen without insistence (a steadfast, persistent devotion). Jivanji Maharaj has shown this kind of insistent devotion in the community of devotees. This insistence has another name — every name of God is good, but you have been given the guru-bestowed name Ramkabir. Just as, for a newborn child, whatever milk suits it from its own mother, no other milk suits it so well. There are shlokas concerning this Ram-Krishna:

_na nandasuno prithagasti raamo na raamato vaa vasudevasunuh ||_
_tathaapyayodhyapurpaalabaale, salakshmane dhaavati me manisha ||19||_

Krishna, the son of Nanda, is not separate from Ram, nor is Ram separate from Vasudev's son Krishna; and yet my mind runs also toward the child protector of the city of Ayodhya, together with Lakshman.

_tatha kaushalaakhye pure raamachandrastatha mathuraakhye yashodaakishorah ||_
_dvayoraikata naiva bhedo vidheyo madeeya manisha yashodaakishore ||20||_

In the same way, Ramchandra of the city called Kaushala, and Yashoda's youthful son of the city called Mathura — there is no distinction between the two, my mind holds; this is what my intellect says regarding Yashoda's son.

Agradas made this bow-bearing Krishna take up the flute again, and at that time the devotee fell at His feet — such is the tribhangi image. Kabirji has said an extraordinary thing —

_kabir kaha kahu chhabi aajki, mein dekhe nandkumaar ||_
_dadhisutaasut upare, saamvadani sang naar ||57||_

Meaning: If one looks at their forms, the two are indeed different, and their deeds are different, but the formless, unblemished Parbrahma is only one. There is no difference between the two, because for a devotee of Parbrahma, there is no distinction such as embodied versus formless — such a devotee does not enter into any dispute. One who is beyond all dispute is truly called a devotee. Furthermore, Kabirji says at the end that Das Kabir only sings Hari's virtues — the supreme duty of a devotee is only to sing the praises of Hari, not to engage in dispute.

_madan gopal hamare shreeraam._
_madan gopal hamare shree raam ||1||_
_itahi dhanush it bimal ben kar ||_
_peetbasan aru tan ghan shyaam ||teka||_
_apni bhuja jene jalnidhi baandhyo ||_
_raas nachaavyo kotik kaam ||_
_tab raghuvar ab jaduvar mohan ||_
_leela lalit bimal sukh dhaam ||_
_bhed rahit das premaanand ||_
_nij jan mali gaaye gun gaan ||_

Meaning: The composer of this pada is the devotee Shri Parmanand (Premanandji). He was a staunch Ramanandi Vaishnav. Once he went to Gokul, and there, early in the morning at the time of the mangal aarti, he came to the palace (temple) of Shri Krishna, the lord of Govardhan. There, the servants (priests) who were present called out and said, "Open the doors of Shri Ramji, it is the time for the mangal aarti."

Then the servants said: "O Parmanandji! Your Ramji lives in Ayodhya — here it is the palace of Madan Gopalji."

Hearing these words, Parmanandji sang the above pada — that to him, there is unity between Ramji and Madan Gopal; there is no distinction for him, no duality here — both are but two different names of the same non-dual form. In truth, both are two different forms of the one Parbrahma, who takes on whatever form is desired and grants darshan accordingly. Parmanand says: without distinction, we sing His virtues together with our own fellow devotees. Thus there is no difference between Ram and Krishna.

Further, Parmanandji says that Parbrahma's leela is truly infinite; it has no end, and moreover, His names too are without end. Thus, understanding Ram and Krishna to be without difference, one should sing the praises of the one Parbrahma alone.

Kabirji too has sung of this very union of Ram-Krishna as the Supreme Lord. Here, explaining the unity of the two forms, Jivanji Maharaj says:

_doi baraabar jeevana. bhagataraaj ranadheer ||_
_kaashi vaasi kabeerji. sarayu teer raghuveer ||38||_
_doi baraabar jeevana. bhagataraaj bhagat bheer ||_
_taat paavan kiyo raghupati. yahaan raamaanand kabeer ||39||_
_saraguN raghupati jeevana. nirguN daas kabeer ||_
_o vishvakun poshataa. o guN bhanjan shareer ||40||_
_prem roop kabeerji. aatam raghupati naam ||_
_jan taravekun jeevana. kali kiyo vishraam ||41||_
_raam svaroopi naam hai. naam svaroopi sant ||_
_kali kaalmaan jeevana. bhajavekun do meet ||42||_
_niravaasik je jeevana. harijan taaka naam ||_
_sarag narak vaikunth taj. je samare seetaraam ||43||_
_nihakaami niramal dasaa. pakade chaarau khoont ||_
_kahe kabeer taa daaski. aash kare vaikunth ||44||_
_sant darashankun jeevana. aas kare vaikunth ||_
_vaikunth baparekee kahaa chali. jo vaanchhe kamalaakanth ||45||_

Meaning: "Doi barabar" means one plus one equals two, and yet equals one: Kabir plus Ram equals one "Ramkabir." Kabirji of Kashi and Ram of the Saryu banks are one and the same. Between these two there is no difference.

Kabir and Ram share much in common. Both are among the foremost of devotees. Both remove the sufferings of their devotees. Through the second, Ram, Dashrath's name became illustrious; while through Kabirji, Ramanand gained even greater fame. Both Dashrath and Ramanand were already renowned through their own deeds, but through Ram and Kabir respectively they became worthy of even greater praise.

Through a son like Ram, a father like Dashrath was made sacred; and through a disciple like Kabir, a sannyasi guru like Ramanand was made illustrious.

Ram is the sustainer and nurturer of the world; therefore Ram fulfills the needs of the world, and so He is called sagun — Ram, being endowed with the three gunas beginning with sattva, is sagun. Kabirji, on the other hand, is beyond the three gunas; he is without any modification, and therefore beyond the gunas — hence Kabir is nirgun. And though dwelling in a body, he has no identification with the body. Thus Ram is sagun and Kabir is nirgun.

Revered Yadunath Maharaj writes that Kabirji is the very image of love, in whom shines the name of God. In the sakhis of Name and Form, Kabir is described as follows:

Baba Kabirji is the very image of love; he moves and acts through the power of the Merciful Lord. If the soul is present, the body rises and stands; and if there were no body, who would sustain the soul?

Therefore, "Vaishnavjan" is the form, and Shri Krishna is the name — thus Kabirji is the form of love, and the name of Ram is the soul that dwells within Kabir. Kabirji has come before us for the very purpose of ferrying across the devotees of this Kali Yuga.

The Name has the form of Ram, and the saint has the form of the Name. In this age of Kali, Jivanji Maharaj advises that taking refuge in this matter of Name and Form alone brings true well-being.

Baba Kabirji says: whichever devotee performs devotion with a desireless attitude, whose mind's state is pure, free from any kind of sin, and who, in every way, holds fast only to the support of God — then even the abode of Vaikunth longs for and waits for such a devotee, hoping that he will one day come to that abode.

Raghupati (Ram) is called sagun, while Kabirji is called nirgun — why? Both are the names of incarnate persons. Though the body, composed of the three gunas, is perishable, Kabirji's nirgun speech is immortal. Thus, holding the nirgun doctrine, Jivanji Maharaj has called Kabirji nirgun, while Ram, the ideal man (Maryada Purushottam), has been called sagun.
